## Research question
How does Marrowline-int8 compare with Selk-MT in translation quality and serving latency?

## Methods summary
Marrowline is our translation model compressed with mixed-precision quantization; Marrowline-int8 and Marrowline-int4 use 8-bit and 4-bit weights, respectively. Selk-MT is the uncompressed fp16 production model that Marrowline is intended to replace.

## Experimental setup
Quality is chrF on the Ombria-News test set (2,500 sentences; higher is better). Latency is per-request wall-clock time measured on one Pellmar P2 inference card while replaying a production trace of 20,000 requests at 40 requests/s; p50 and p99 are the median and 99th-percentile request latencies.

## Experiments and comparisons
- `exp1`: Quality and latency of compressed vs production model
  - comparison `exp1/cmp1`: Marrowline-int8 vs Selk-MT: chrF, p50 and p99 latency
  - comparison `exp1/cmp2`: Marrowline-int4 vs Selk-MT: chrF, p50 and p99 latency

## Results tables

sentences.text: On the Ombria-News test set, Marrowline-int8 achieves slightly lower translation quality than Selk-MT (chrF 57.9 vs 58.4), though no statistical test was reported for this difference.
Marrowline-int8 also provides substantially lower serving latency than Selk-MT, with p50 latency of 97 ms vs 186 ms and p99 latency of 610 ms vs 1,240 ms on the replayed production trace.
Marrowline-int4 shows a larger quality drop (chrF 55.2 vs 58.4) but even lower latency (p50 71 ms, p99 460 ms) compared to Selk-MT.
On the Ombria-News test set, Marrowline-int8 achieves slightly lower translation quality than Selk-MT (chrF 57.9 vs 58.4), though no statistical test was reported for this difference.

Marrowline-int8 also provides lower serving latency than Selk-MT, with p50 latency of 97 ms vs 186 ms and p99 latency of 610 ms vs 1,240 ms on the replayed production trace, though no statistical test was reported for this difference.
Marrowline-int4 shows a larger quality drop (chrF 55.2 vs 58.4) but even lower latency (p50 71 ms, p99 460 ms) compared to Selk-MT.
On the Ombria-News test set, Marrowline-int8 achieved a chrF of 57.9 versus 58.4 for Selk-MT, a decrease of 0.5 points.
In serving latency on the replayed production trace, Marrowline-int8 reduced p50 latency from 186 ms to 97 ms and p99 latency from 1,240 ms to 610 ms compared with Selk-MT.
No statistical tests were reported, so the observed differences cannot be distinguished from chance variation.
These findings are specific to the Ombria-News test set and the Pellmar P2 trace; generalizability is unknown.

These results indicate that Marrowline-int8 offers substantially lower latency with only a small quality loss relative to the uncompressed production model, although no statistical tests were reported to assess the reliability of these differences.
